newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's TIM reduces GSM phone charges.
newsitem.headline: Italy's TIM reduces GSM phone charges.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled mobile phone operator Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) said it was introducing a new zero subscription GSM service and reducing some tariffs on existing services.
TIM said its new Eurobasic formula aimed at business clients would not carry a monthly subscription charge and would have a single tariff for calls of 700 lire per minute 24 hours a day.

It also said in a statement it was cutting charges for its three existing GSM services -- EuroProfessional, EuroFamily and EuroTime -- consisting of reductions in monthly subscription charges and discounts on call tariffs.
From June 1, TIM said it will be moving to a system of charging calls timed to the second instead of a unit basis.
